title.narrative: Road Network Upgrading Project

description.narrative: The project will (i) reconstruct or upgrade and climate proof about 59 kilometers (km) of principal national roads, (ii) expand the road maintenance program of the Ministry of Infrastructure (MOI), and (iii) prepare a feasibility study and detailed design for 81 km of principal national roads. In collaboration with other development partners, the project will support the progressive upgrading of the whole of the national road network.

title.narrative: 26 Jun 2015 | News Release: https://www.adb.org/news/timor-leste-road-project-gets-additional-12-million-funding-boost
Grant 0504: 93% of contracts awarded and 74% disbursed as of 21 Apr 2025
Loan 2857: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 21 Apr 2025
Loan 2858: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 21 Apr 2025
Loan 3181: 96% of contracts awarded and 94% disbursed as of 21 Apr 2025

Progress Toward Outcome: Works under Grant 0504 for C16/17 Package 1, C13, and C16/17 Package 2 road sections commenced in 2019. Completion of Grant 0504 has been extended to 31 December 2023 to allow completion of civil works, coverage of defect liability period under the grant, and preparation of project completion report.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Jun 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/45094/45094-001-apfs-en_8.pdf
Some results are in the Initial Environmental Examination | Dec 2023: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/45094/45094-001-iee-en_0.pdf
Some results are in the Proactive Integrity Reviews (PIR) | Dec 2018: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/45094/45094-001-pprr-en.pdf
Some results are in the Resettlement Plans | Jan 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/45094/45094-001-rp-en_1.pdf
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | Apr 2025: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/45094/45094-001-smr-en_11.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: Feasibility studies have been completed in January 2015.

Data for Grant 0504 shows a total 126 male workers equivalent to 70.79% of total 178 workers, and 9 females workers equivalent to 13.69% of total workers have attended HIV/AIDS awareness education sessions.
Actual achievement to be assessed.
Roads under L2857/2858 which were completed in 2016 were under PBM. R3: Tibar-Liquica Road Section (20.15km), and R4A: Tibar Gleno Road Section (31.90km)
Civil works for Tibar Port- Liquica (20.15km) completed on 15 August 2016; PBM completed in August 2018. Civil works for Tibar to Gleno (31.90km) completed on 30 April 2016; PBM completed in May 2018.
Civil works for Tasitolou to Tibar road section 100% completed on 16 Aug 2021. Defects liability period from 17 Aug 2021 to 16 Aug 2022. This will be followed by 24 months performance-based maintenance from Aug 2022 to Aug 2024. Formal request for extension of L3181-TIM closing date is expected to be received from the government.
The total completed roads under Loans 2857/2858 (52.05km) and Loan 3181 (4.50km) is 56.55km with roughness of about 4m/km.
Following government's request, Loan 3181's closing date has been extended to 30 December 2023. Another extension request is expected to be received which will cover the 24 months performance-based maintenance period from August 2022 to August 2024.
Under Grant 0504, total of 31.43km completed as of August 2022 with the following breakdown: C13 - 98.36% complete; C16/17 Package 1 -100% complete (completed in June 2020); and C16/17 Package 2 - 39.37% complete (based on latest progress update, as of 25 August 2022 from MPW/PMU received in September 2022).
Note that as per civil works contracts, the total km for completion is 41.34km (93.95% of target 44kms) composed of 11.81km under C13; 13.50km under C16/17 Package 1; and 16.03km under C16/17 Package 2.
On 14 April 2021, ADB provided no objection to the proposed contract variation for additional works under civil works contract C16/17 Package 2 to include the following:
(i) Construction of the 2.52-km missing link between C16/17 Package 1 (station 32+045) and C16/17 Package 2 (station 0+000) road sections;
(ii) Overlaying the existing pavement of about 100 meters to connect the public services area (i.e., sub-district administrator office, health, school, and other public facility/buildings) to the project road at station 14+60 at C16/17 Package 1; and
(iii) Additional pavement works to widen total of 7.5km of C16/17 Package 1 road section from station 4+000 to station 11+500 from 3 meters to 5 meters by adding 1 meter each on both sides of road shoulder.
ADB's no objection to the proposed variation order was on the condition that the government will carry out due diligence to identify any environmental and/or land acquisition and resettlement impacts associated with the additional works by June 2021. Based on the findings of the due diligence, corresponding safeguards assessments and plans shall be prepared and submitted to ADB for review and clearance before any construction activities take place
Following government's request, Grant 0504's closing date has been extended to 31 December 2023.
On 28 May 2021, ADB received letter from MPW seeking no objection to proposed VO.3 to C13 civil works contract with an increase in contract amount of $1,081,480.30 due to discrepancy between the BOQ and design drawings and extension of time for completion. On 12 July 2021, a VC bet ADB (HQ, and TLRM), and MPW/PMU was held to discuss the request. ADB explained to MPW/PMU that the uncommitted amount under Category 0301-Works and Consulting Services is already fully 'allocated for two previously ADB-endorsed variation orders for the contracts of the construction supervision consultants, and C16/17 Package 2 road section contractor and ADB is awaiting receipt of signed VOs issued to the consultant and contractor before ADB could update the contract amounts in LFIS. ADB also mentioned that the current $300,832.43 uncommitted under Category 1600- Misc Grant Admin & Support costs-ADB is to be reallocated to Category 0301- Works and Consulting Services to partially finance the $543,054.29 shortfall due to the two endorsed variation orders. Furthermore, ADB informed MPW/PMU that the fund needed to increase the C13 civil works contract is currently locked in Category 1600- Misc Grant Admin & Support costs-ADB and the only way to reduce this is through disbursements. MPW/PMU in response informed ADB that it will discus the matter with MPW and subsequently inform ADB on which contract (i.e., C16/17 Package 2 contract or C13 contract) will be prioritized for variation.
MPW/PMU through a supplement letter dated 28 July 2021, informed ADB that it would like to prioritize the items proposed under VO.3 for C13 civil works contract over variation order number 2 for C16/17 Package 2 civil works contract. ADB is currently processing the request for variation order number 3 to C13 civil works contract.
On 14 Oct 2021, ADB provided no objection to VO.3 to C13 civil works contract. MPW/PMU was informed that it can only issue variation order number 2 to C16/17 Package 2 only after the uncommitted grant funds become sufficient (i.e., after another reallocation to Cat 3201 from Cat 1600 will be completed).
Local workers are hired by contactors based on the location of the road sections.
Majority of workers come from local areas where the road sections are located. Based on construction supervision consultant reports, residents in specific Sucos do not allow other workers coming from other Sucos to work within their area. This has even resulted to delays in the project's progress.
Exact number of local workers including % of women and % involved in bioengineering work have yet to be determined/assessed.
